svg.title: A hash table keeps empty space on purpose
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing four hash buckets with the keys ann, bob and cy hashed and masked into them and the arithmetic written out; a fourth key dee colliding and being hung off a bucket as a chain at 1.15 probes; the same collision resolved by open addressing with numbered probes walking right two occupied slots before landing in a free one; a resize where the four-bucket table is crossed out in red and every key is redrawn into an eight-bucket table because the mask changed; and a plot of average probes against load factor where chaining stays nearly flat from 1.15 to 1.50 while open addressing climbs from 1.22 to 40.99, with a worst observed probe count of 15,832.
svg.text: A hash table keeps empty space on purpose
the mask only works because capacity
is a power of two. That is the only
reason it is a power of two.
the bucket is a tiny list. Nothing else moves.
probe, probe, land - the key lives in someone else's bucket
which is why deleting needs a tombstone, not a hole
you cannot copy buckets across. The mask changed
from & 3 to & 7, so every key belongs somewhere
5. and the dial that decides all of it
worst probe actually observed: 8 (chaining) vs 15,832 (open addressing)
...and if an ATTACKER picks the keys? 4,649x
